tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend...') and focuses on user intent/triggers rather than implementation details. It explicitly lists many trigger contexts (high/low bills, token drift, pricing tiers, cost per team, quota headroom, throttling, etc.) covering cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly, and ends with an explicit exclusion ('Not for outages happening now.'). While long, it is a single flowing sentence enumerating scope rather than verbose prose, consistent with being 'pushy' about applicability as the best-practice calls for.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what is CloudWatch, what is cost) and jumps straight into project-specific rules, domain procedures, and non-obvious edge cases (e.g., exclusive End dates, mantle usage types, token reconciliation). It's dense but every sentence conveys non-obvious, domain-specific information the agent wouldn't otherwise know.
tests.evidence: "Usage types vary (-mantle-, -standard, -flex, -priority, -cross-region-global): match a model's lines loosely."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains rules, routing tables, and short per-check summaries but defers detailed reference data (full API quirks, metric definitions, cost analysis derivations, quota code lookups) to references/ files, linked conditionally in the router table and steps.
tests.evidence: "Router: How to read each API and metric: [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) (load it with any row)."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links in the body: api-quirks.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, cost-analysis.md, metrics-and-logs.md, quota-codes.md, related-skills.md.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific trigger/condition (step number, check-id, or scenario), telling the agent when to load it.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references/ file links use relative paths from the skill root with the 'references/' prefix, no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (cost labeling, pricing sourcing, quota lookups, PT resizing) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible areas (scoping, how to handle ambiguous regions) allow judgment with rationale given.
tests.evidence: "PT can't be resized in place (UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput changes only the name or model): give the LLM-PT-001 remediation, never an update command."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple approaches exist (e.g., price source order, quota lookup paths) the skill establishes a clear ordered default with fallbacks rather than presenting equal options.
tests.evidence: "Rates, in order: the user (say so); pricing:GetProducts ... or the pricing page read with verify_aws_claim."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (Steps 1-8) for reviewing capacity/cost across any model/region/account, not a one-off instance; specific details like exact API calls and templates support the reusable approach.
tests.evidence: "Step 1: Scope: region(s), window, models and profiles; state the defaults chosen (current region, trailing window)."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' listing non-obvious API/metric pitfalls specific to Bedrock cost/capacity analysis.
tests.evidence: "'A us. profile bills as us-east-1.' It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region (api-quirks §14, LLM-COST-005)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides a dedicated report template asset for full reports, satisfying the structured-output need.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; the only report template is stored in assets/ and referenced, not embedded.
tests.evidence: The body contains no inline report template skeleton; it only links to the asset template.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is explicitly linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the condition under which to load it (only for a full report), satisfying the when-to-load requirement.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with the 'assets/' prefix.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow 'Procedure — Capacity & Cost Review' is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' format, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Scope: region(s), window, models and profiles..." through "- [ ] Step 8: Assemble the findings..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section ('Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output') instructing the agent to check its own output against rules before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so."
